 LIHEAP expected to handle increasing home heating costs
 HALEY DAUGHERTY 
 TribLive
 Sat, Nov 14, 2026 • 06:00 AM 
 Share 
 Copy Link 
 Email 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Send SMS 
 WhatsApp 
 Reddit 
 Like 
 (AP)
 Officials for the state’s Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program say funding for the program is expected to be adequate this year despite skyrocketing prices for electricity, natural gas and home heating oil.
 The federally funded program assists eligible families financially to heat their homes during the winter.
 According to September statistics released by the National Energy Assistance Directors Association, the price of heating oil is projected to increase more than 31% from last winter.
 “Heating oil costs are projected to rise by 31.3%, largely because of the sharp increase in heating oil prices driven by the war in Iran,” the report said.
 Electricity is projected to increase by 9%, natural gas by nearly 6% and propane by almost 9%.
 NEADA is advocating for LIHEAP funding to be increased in response to rising prices. The report calls for a federal funding increase from $4 billion to $7 billion.
 Despite rising costs and national calls for more funding, the state’s Department of Human Services is not concerned about its level of funding this season.
 “The current LIHEAP season opened on Nov. 2, and while it is too early to know if we will receive more applications than last year, PA DHS expects to have adequate funding for this LIHEAP season, which runs through April 23, 2027,” said Brandon Cwalina, spokesperson for the state Department of Human Services.
 The program assists almost 300,000 people per year, Cwalina said.
 Assistance is available to households in a couple forms, according to Duquesne Light Co. The first being cash grants, a one-time lump sum based on household size, income and heating fuel type. Cash grants are limited to one utility, according to Duquesne Light.
 The program lasts until April 23, and applicants are eligible to receive between $200 and $1,000, according to the state.
 During the 2025-26 LIHEAP season, just under 280,000 households statewide received LIHEAP cash benefits, and these households received an average season benefit of $289, according to the state Department of Human Services.
 “LIHEAP is one of the strongest tools we have to help Pennsylvania families stay warm and manage their energy bills,” Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission Chairman Steve DeFrank said in a statement. “We encourage anyone who may be struggling to apply early and also reach out to their utilities.”
 Additional assistance is also available in the form of crisis grants for households experiencing a heating emergency or in immediate danger of being without heat.
 Crisis grants can be used with more than one utility, up to the maximum grant amount. Grant amounts are determined by the amount needed to resolve the emergency.
 About 121,000 households statewide received LIHEAP crisis benefits, and these households received an average payment of $566, according to Pennsylvania DHS.
 “Pennsylvanians need to be able to heat their homes and keep themselves and their families warm through the winter, and LIHEAP helps hundreds of thousands of Pennsylvanians each year stay safe and healthy during the coldest months of the year,” state DHS Secretary Val Arkoosh said in a statement. “Anyone who may need help with heating costs and keeping their home safe through this winter should apply for LIHEAP as soon as possible.”
